title: token_compression_runtime_wiring
goal: wire token-compression primitives through shadow-first runtime gates without changing default capture contracts
constraints: default command capture output must remain unchanged unless an explicit opt-in is enabled
shadow assembly must not feed the model or write public telemetry
public JSON, log, schema, policy, quarantine, and replay contracts stay stable until additive contract slices land
high-uncertainty reduction must retain source evidence or fall back to the existing capture path
avoid hidden downloads, slow disk scans, and storage-compression work in the capture control plane

slices.goal: document the Phase XI shadow-first rollout contract, acceptance gates, rollback rule, and public-surface boundaries
run typed assembly in a private shadow path and prove returned capture text, status, stats, and public contracts remain unchanged
add an explicit opt-in prompt profile for narrow command classes only after shadow evidence is fixture-backed
collect non-public fixture measurements for omission counts, recall, replay recoverability, and size deltas
document whether typed assembly should remain opt-in, expand through additive surfaces, or defer default wiring

decision.summary: keep typed assembly runtime wiring behind the explicit shadow_narrow prompt profile only
rationale: default capture output and public contracts remain intentionally unchanged
fixture-backed evidence exists only for the narrow test_output and git_diff reducer classes
rollback remains one env toggle and preserves the existing run -> reduce -> clip path
public telemetry, quarantine, replay, and schema surfaces should change only through additive contract work
follow_on: expand fixture-backed recall and fallback coverage before widening reducer eligibility
introduce additive diagnostics or telemetry only with explicit contract fixtures and changelog coverage
defer any default prompt replacement until opt-in operation proves stable across a broader command corpus
